claims.vo: It looked like any other bill.

sources.quote: deceptive mailers that falsely appeared to their recipients—primarily small businesses that already had websites—to be invoices for purported web hosting services.

claims.vo: A due date. An amount due: one hundred eighty dollars. A line that read, Yearly Web Hosting.

sources.quote: it listed a due date, the amount due, a description of the services provided, i.e. "Yearly Web Hosting,"
sources.note: Indictment (allegation); corroborated by the DOJ-published exemplar on the case page [2a]: "DUE DATE: 5/11/19" · "Amount 180.00" · "Yearly Web Hosting".

sources.quote: The invoices typically listed $180 as the amount due.

claims.vo: It went mostly to small businesses that already had a website.

sources.quote: primarily small businesses that already had websites

claims.vo: Their sites were hosted by someone else. The company on the bill had never hosted them.

sources.quote: Those victims, whose websites were hosted by other providers, received nothing from the defendant except another "invoice," a year later, asking for more money.
